subject: Slate Partners — tenor flexibility & GPU cost-share proposal
messages:
From: Dana Liu <dana@slatepartners.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@slatepartners.com>, Legal <legal@slatepartners.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Reserved capacity ask — term flexibility tied to GPU cost moves

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited about Redwood's latency profile but the CFO pushed back on a straight 36-month commit given today's GPU market volatility. Two asks from our side: 1) can Redwood offer a tenor-flex option that phases committed vCPU/GPU over 24–36 months; and 2) can we build a price-sensitivity mechanism so Slate doesn't bear full GPU-cost volatility (e.g., a shared-cost corridor or capped pass-through)?

We are planning to size for 350 A100-equivalent vGPUs at peak, with a staggered ramp across Q1–Q4 2029. Procurement/Legal are on this thread — they want an outline of guardrails for discounts and what internal approvals Redwood would need for any below-list pricing.

Can you share a draft proposal and a couple of sizing/pricing scenarios? If we can align on a flexible tenor + limited cost pass-through, execs are comfortable moving to an LOI.

— Dana

[Attachment: slate_capacity_estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)]

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana@slatepartners.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Nov 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — term flexibility tied to GPU cost moves

Dana — thanks, and great context. High level response: yes, we can structure a phased reserved commitment and surface a pricing-sensitivity construct, but the commercial cadence and approval ladder differ depending on the depth of the discount and the degree of pass-through.

Quick items I'll include in a short proposal for you by EOD Friday:
- Three sizing ramps: Conservative (200 vGPU), Target (350 vGPU), Aggressive (500 vGPU) with month-by-month activation windows.
- Two pricing constructs: (A) fixed discount tiers by committed vGPU/year (standard approvals), (B) indexed corridor where Redwood shares GPU-cost delta above a baseline up to a cap (requires finance & sales leadership sign-off for >20% discount exposure).
- Suggested contract language for phased activation and a 12–month check-in to rebase forecasts.

Cc—Marcus: can you run sensitivity models for the three ramps and show the discount bandwidth required to guarantee break-even for Redwood if market GPU costs increase 30% vs baseline?
Cc—Kimberly: this is likely an approval that would need your team if we hit the indexed corridor scenario.

Attaching a straw MOU + a quick workbook with the ramp sketch.

Next steps: Dana, if that aligns I'll follow up with the MOU + a short note that flags the approval thresholds so procurement/legal can see sign-off flow.

Thanks,
Avery

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Nov 2028 10:25:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity ask — term flexibility tied to GPU cost moves

Quick sensitivity summary (see attached workbook 'Sized_Fleet_Scenario_A.xlsx'):

Assumptions: baseline GPU cost = $1.20/tokenized-unit (internal metric), current market variance +/- 35% observed. Pricing is expressed as cost per vGPU-hour equivalent.

Scenarios (annualized):
- Conservative (200 vGPU): Base price with 12% list discount. If GPU costs +30%, Redwood EF margin compresses by ~9 p.p.; to avoid negative margin we need to surface an additional 6% rebate or corridor share.
- Target (350 vGPU): Base price with 16% list discount. At +30% GPU cost, margin compresses ~11 p.p.; to hold target margin require ~9% compensatory mechanism.
- Aggressive (500 vGPU): Base price with 20% list discount (requires director-level approval). At +30% GPU cost, margin compresses ~14 p.p.; fallback is to limit corridor exposure to 50% of delta beyond baseline and cap aggregate exposure at 8% of ARR.

Approval ladder suggestion:
- Up to 10% effective discount: AE + Revenue Ops sign-off.
- 10%	6% (1025%): Sales leadership approval.
- >25% effective discount or >8% ARR pass-through exposure: VP/Finance & Revenue Exec approval required.

I recommend we present two packaged options to Slate: (1) Standard phased commit with modest list discounts; (2) Index-corridor option where Redwood and Slate split GPU-cost delta 50/50 up to a 10% cap, with a rebase after 12 months. Option 2 will require executive approvals if the implied discount crosses 15% effective.

Flagging: legal language needs a clearly defined formula for the GPU index, lookback period, and an upper bound on pass-through exposure.

-Marcus

[Attachment: Sized_Fleet_Scenario_A.xlsx (spreadsheet, 210KB)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Nov 2028 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity ask — term flexibility tied to GPU cost moves

Thanks Marcus 11 good analysis. Decision guidance: we can approve an index-corridor structure with the following constraints:

1) Maximum company exposure (pass-through to Redwood) capped at 8% of the first-year ARR for the Slate deal.
2) Any structure that implies >15% effective discount relative to our list must be routed to me and Finance (i.e., VP approval).
3) Corridor split default = 50/50 (Redwood/Slate); if Slate requests 60/40 in their favor we can consider only if they commit to an accelerated ramp (>= 400 vGPU by month 12).
4) Legal must include a 12-month rebase clause and an audit clause for GPU cost index inputs.

Avery: you can present Option 1 (standard phased commit) and Option 2 (index-corridor with the constraints above). If Slate signs an LOI for Option 2 we will prepare an exec approval packet that quantifies ARR exposure.

Kimberly
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Slate Partners proposal & next steps (MOU + sign path)

Dana 11 thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a short MOU that captures two commercial options for Slate Partners:

Option A — Phased Reserved Commitment (standard):
- 24	6-month activation window, commit tiers at 200 / 350 / 500 vGPU levels.
- Standard list discounts (106% depending on tier).
- 12-month forecast rebase and quarterly usage reporting.

Option B — Index-Corridor (shared GPU cost exposure):
- Same phased activation; corridor defined against baseline GPU index (see MOU section 3).
- 50/50 split of GPU-cost delta above baseline up to an 8% ARR exposure cap (Redwood internal approval required if effective discount >15%).
- 12-month rebase and audit rights for index inputs.

Requested next steps:
1) Please review the attached MOU and the sizing workbook.
2) If Option B is interesting, confirm you can accept the 8% first-year ARR cap and the 50/50 split (or indicate preference for an accelerated ramp to support a larger Slate-favorable split).
3) If aligned, sign the MOU (DocuSign link below) and we'll schedule a 30-minute sync to walk procurement/legal through the index formula and the approval path.

DocuSign (MOU v1): https://docusign.net/Signer?envelopeId=1234-EXAMPLE

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through.
